title: Italian A2 — Everyday Life
shortDescription: The next step after A1: talk about your day, your past and your plans, handle the doctor and offices — and prepare for the CILS A2 exam.
description:
For learners who finished A1 (or already know the basics). In 8 weekly units you learn to describe your routine, tell stories in the past (passato prossimo and imperfetto), talk about your home, your life before Italy, your health and your plans for the future, and make polite requests in offices with the conditional.

Every unit has picture words with audio, one clear grammar point with exercises, a speaking role-play where you answer out loud, and a review with a printable study sheet. A2 is the level required for the long-term EU residence permit.
objectives:
Describe your daily routine with reflexive verbs
Talk about the past with the passato prossimo and the imperfetto
Describe your home and solve problems with the landlord
Explain symptoms and understand the doctor's instructions
Talk about plans with the future tense
Make polite requests with the conditional and prepare for CILS A2

lessons.title: Reflexive verbs
lessons.summary: mi sveglio, ti alzi, si veste: actions you do to yourself.

blocks.title: I verbi riflessivi
blocks.body:
A **reflexive verb** describes an action you do to yourself. In the dictionary it ends in **-si**: *svegliarsi* (to wake up), *lavarsi* (to wash), *vestirsi* (to get dressed).

Put the small word **mi, ti, si, ci, vi, si** before the verb:
- *Mi sveglio presto.* = I wake up early.
- *A che ora ti alzi?* = What time do you get up?

How often: **sempre** (always), **di solito** (usually), **spesso** (often), **qualche volta** (sometimes), **non … mai** (never).

lessons.title: The past with "avere"
lessons.summary: ho mangiato, hai lavorato: talking about finished actions.

blocks.title: Il passato prossimo con avere
blocks.body:
The **passato prossimo** is the most common past tense. Use the present of **avere** + the **past participle**:

- verbs in **-are** → **-ato**: lavorare → *lavorato*
- verbs in **-ere** → **-uto**: vendere → *venduto*
- verbs in **-ire** → **-ito**: dormire → *dormito*

Some common verbs are irregular: **fare → fatto**, **vedere → visto**, **prendere → preso**, **leggere → letto**, **scrivere → scritto**, **bere → bevuto**.

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: Time words like **ieri**, **sabato scorso**, **un mese fa** tell you it's the past — then use the passato prossimo.

lessons.title: The past with "essere"
lessons.summary: sono andato, sei arrivata: verbs of movement and change.

blocks.title: Il passato prossimo con essere
blocks.body:
Some verbs form the passato prossimo with **essere** instead of avere. They are mostly verbs of **movement** and **change**: andare, venire, partire, arrivare, tornare, uscire, entrare, restare, nascere, diventare — and all **reflexive verbs** (*mi sono svegliato*).

With essere, the participle **agrees** like an adjective:
- **-o** man, **-a** woman, **-i** men/mixed group, **-e** women
- *Ahmed è andato.* · *Priya è andata.* · *Siamo andati.* · *Le ragazze sono andate.*

blocks.title: I pronomi diretti
blocks.body:
Direct object pronouns replace a thing or a person, so you don't repeat it. They go **before** the verb:

- *Compri il pane?* — *Sì, **lo** compro.* (Yes, I buy it.)
- *Lavi la macchina?* — *Sì, **la** lavo.*
- *Chiami i tuoi genitori?* — *Sì, **li** chiamo ogni sera.*
- *Stiri le camicie?* — *No, non **le** stiro.*

People: **mi** (me), **ti** (you), **ci** (us), **vi** (you all): *Mi chiami domani?* (Will you call me tomorrow?)

lessons.title: The imperfetto
lessons.summary: lavoravo, abitavo, era: how things used to be.

blocks.title: L'imperfetto
blocks.body:
Use the **imperfetto** for:
- **habits** in the past: *Ogni giorno andavo a scuola a piedi.* (I used to walk to school)
- **descriptions**: *La casa era grande.* (The house was big)
- **age, time, weather**: *Avevo dieci anni. Faceva caldo.*

Use the **passato prossimo** for a single, finished event: *Nel 2022 sono arrivato in Italia.*

The imperfetto is very regular: take away **-re** and add **-vo, -vi, -va, -vamo, -vate, -vano**. Only **essere** is irregular: *ero, eri, era, eravamo, eravate, erano*.

lessons.title: The formal imperative
lessons.summary: Prenda, si sieda, beva: understanding instructions.

blocks.title: L'imperativo formale (Lei)
blocks.body:
Doctors, pharmacists and officials give instructions with the **formal imperative** (Lei):

- verbs in **-are** → **-i**: *aspettare → Aspetti!* (wait), *respirare → Respiri!* (breathe)
- verbs in **-ere / -ire** → **-a**: *prendere → Prenda!* (take), *aprire → Apra la bocca!* (open your mouth)

Common irregular forms: **venga** (come), **vada** (go), **faccia** (do), **dica** (say/tell), **beva** (drink), **si sieda** (sit down), **stia** (stay/be).

Negative: **non** + the same form: *Non beva alcol.*

blocks.title: Il futuro semplice
blocks.body:
In everyday Italian the **present** is often used for the near future: *Domani vado a Milano.* For plans, predictions and promises, use the **futuro semplice**.

Regular endings: **-rò, -rai, -rà, -remo, -rete, -ranno**. Verbs in **-are** change the *a* to **e**: *lavorare → lavorerò*.

Common irregular verbs: **essere → sarò**, **avere → avrò**, **andare → andrò**, **fare → farò**, **venire → verrò**, **potere → potrò**, **dovere → dovrò**.

lessons.title: Polite requests: the conditional
lessons.summary: vorrei, potrei, potrebbe: asking politely.

blocks.title: Il condizionale di cortesia
blocks.body:
The **conditional** makes requests polite — essential in offices, shops and with employers.

- **vorrei** = I would like (*Vorrei un appuntamento.*)
- **potrei** = could I (*Potrei parlare con il responsabile?*)
- **potrebbe** = could you, formal (*Potrebbe ripetere, per favore?*)
- **dovrei** = I should (*Dovrei rinnovare il permesso.*)
- **mi piacerebbe** = I would like to (*Mi piacerebbe fare il corso B1.*)

The endings are **-rei, -resti, -rebbe, -remmo, -reste, -rebbero** — on the same stem as the future: *farò → farei*, *sarò → sarei*.
